paragraphs: ## A Piece of Wood
Once upon a time there was a piece of wood. It was not a fine piece. It was only an ordinary log, the kind that people burn in the fire in winter.

An old carpenter called Master Cherry found it in his shop. His nose was round and red like a ripe cherry, and that is why everybody used this name. He took his axe and lifted it to cut the wood. Then he heard a tiny voice. "Please don't hit me so hard!"

Master Cherry's eyes grew wide. He looked round the room. Nobody was there. He looked under the table, in the cupboard and in the basket of wood chips. Nobody was there. "I am getting old," he said. "My ears are playing a game with me." He took the axe again. And again the voice cried, "Ow! You hurt me!"

Now the carpenter was really afraid. At that moment someone knocked at the door. It was his old friend Geppetto. Geppetto always wore a yellow wig. The boys of the street called him Polenta because of it, and this made him very angry.

"Good morning, Master Cherry," said Geppetto. "I have an idea. I want to make a beautiful puppet out of wood. It will dance, fight with a sword and jump through the air. I will take it round the world and earn a piece of bread and a glass of wine."

"I have the right thing for you," said Master Cherry. He was glad to give the strange log away. And the little voice said, "Thank you!" Master Cherry thought that Geppetto was making a joke, and he became angry. The two old friends had a quarrel. Soon they made peace, and Geppetto went home with the log under his arm.

Geppetto lived in a poor little room under the stairs. The only light came from a small window. There was a bad chair, a bad bed and a broken table. On the wall there was a fireplace with a fire and a pot of boiling water. But the fire and the pot were only a picture.
Geppetto took his tools and started to work. "What name shall I give him?" he said. "I will call him Pinocchio. It is a lucky name."

First he made the hair, then the forehead, then the eyes. The eyes were strange. They moved, and then they looked straight at him. "Why do you look at me, wooden eyes?" he said. Nobody answered. Next he made the nose. At once it began to grow. It grew and grew until it was very long. Geppetto cut it, but the more he cut, the longer it became.

Then he made the mouth. It was not finished when it began to laugh and put out its tongue. "Stop laughing!" said Geppetto. But the mouth went on laughing. Then the hands pulled the yellow wig off his head. "You are a bad boy," he said sadly, "and you are not even finished!"

Last he made the legs and the feet. As soon as they were ready, Pinocchio gave him a kick on the end of his nose. "It is my fault," said Geppetto. "I should have thought of this before." He took the puppet by the hands and taught him to walk. Pinocchio learned very quickly. Soon he was running about the room. Then he found the door open. He ran out into the street and away.

Poor Geppetto ran after him, but he could not catch him. "Stop him! Stop him!" he shouted. A policeman heard the noise and took Pinocchio by the nose. He gave the puppet back to Geppetto. Geppetto wanted to pull his ear, but he could not find one. He forgot to make ears! So he took him by the neck. "Come home," he said. "I will teach you a lesson."

The people in the street began to talk. "That Geppetto looks kind, but he is hard with children," they said. "The poor puppet will be hurt." The policeman believed them and put poor Geppetto in prison. Pinocchio ran home, laughing.
## The Talking Cricket
Pinocchio was alone in the house. Suddenly a voice said, "Cri-cri-cri!" It was a small cricket on the wall.
"Pinocchio, listen to me," said the cricket. "Boys who do not obey their fathers and run away from home will always be sorry. Go to school and learn something."
"I don't want to go to school," said Pinocchio. "I want to eat, drink, sleep and play all day."
"If you do this, you will end in prison or in the hospital."
"Be quiet, old cricket!" cried Pinocchio. He took a wooden hammer and threw it at the cricket. The poor cricket did not even have time to say "cri". It was dead against the wall.

Soon Pinocchio began to feel hungry. There was nothing to eat in the house. He found an egg and wanted to cook it. But when he broke it, a little chicken jumped out. "Thank you for breaking my house," it said, and it flew out of the window.

Pinocchio went out to beg for bread, but nobody gave him any. At last an old man poured a bucket of cold water on his head from a window. He came home wet and tired. He put his feet on a pot of hot coals and fell asleep. In the night his wooden feet burned away.

In the morning Geppetto came home. The policeman had let him out of prison. "Father, I can't walk!" cried Pinocchio. Geppetto was kind. He made him new feet. "Father," said Pinocchio, "I will go to school. I will learn and I will be good."

But a boy needs a school book. Geppetto had no money. So he sold his only coat, and it was winter. He bought the book and gave it to Pinocchio. "Where is your coat, Father?" "I sold it. I was too hot." Pinocchio understood. He cried and kissed his father.
## The Puppet Theatre

The next morning Pinocchio went to school with the book under his arm. On the way he heard music: drums and trumpets. There was a puppet theatre in the square. "What is that?" he asked a boy. "Buy a ticket and see!"
Pinocchio did not have any money. He sold his school book and bought a ticket.

Inside, the puppets were acting on the stage. When they saw Pinocchio, they shouted, "It is Pinocchio! He is our brother!" The play stopped. The theatre owner came out. He was a huge man with a black beard as long as a river. His name was Fire-Eater. He was so terrible that everybody shook.
"Who made this noise?" he shouted. He took Pinocchio in his big hand. "Tonight I want to roast my lamb. I need dry wood for the fire. Put him in the fire!"
Pinocchio began to cry. Then Harlequin, one of the puppets, said, "Please, master, don't burn him!" "No," said Fire-Eater. "I want his wood for my fire."

Then Pinocchio said, "Please burn me and not Harlequin. I am ready." Fire-Eater was moved. When he was moved, he always sneezed. He sneezed loudly. "Ah-choo! You are a good puppet," he said. "Tell me, who is your father?"

Pinocchio told him about Geppetto and the coat. Fire-Eater gave him five gold coins. "Take them to your father," he said. "Give him my greetings." Pinocchio thanked him, kissed all the puppets and went away, very happy.
## The Fox and the Cat
Half a mile down the road, Pinocchio met a Fox who walked with a limp and a Cat who was blind. They walked together like good friends.
"Good morning, Pinocchio," said the Fox. "Where are you going with that money?" Pinocchio told them everything. He said that he wanted to buy his father a new coat.

"Do you want to double your gold?" said the Fox. "Come with us to the Field of Miracles. You dig a small hole. You put your coins in it and cover them with earth. You add a little water and some salt. In the morning there will be a beautiful tree with a thousand gold coins on it."
Pinocchio thought about the tree. He forgot his father, the school and the cricket's words. "Let's go!" he said.

That evening they stopped at an inn called the Red Lobster. They ate a big dinner, and Pinocchio went to bed. "Wake him at midnight," the Fox told the innkeeper. "We must go on." But at midnight the innkeeper said, "Your friends left an hour ago. They said that you should follow them in the morning."

Pinocchio walked into the dark night alone. Then he heard a voice. It was the cricket's ghost. "Go home, Pinocchio," it said. "Boys who want to be rich in one day always come to a bad end." Pinocchio did not listen.

Suddenly two men in black sacks jumped out of the trees. "Your money or your life!" Pinocchio had hidden the gold coins under his tongue. He could not speak, so he shook his head. They tried to open his mouth. He bit one of them, and the hand was a cat's paw! He ran away, but the two men chased him and caught him. They tied a rope round his neck and hung him from a branch of the Big Oak. "We will come back tomorrow," they said.
## The Blue Fairy

At that moment a little girl with blue hair looked out of the window of a white house. She clapped her hands, and a great falcon came. "Go and cut that puppet down from the tree," she said. The falcon flew away and soon Pinocchio was lying on a bed in the white house.

The Fairy called three doctors: a Crow, an Owl and the Talking Cricket. They said that he needed some medicine. But the medicine was bitter, and Pinocchio did not want to take it. Then four black rabbits came in with a coffin. "Take the medicine," said the Fairy, "or they will take you." Pinocchio drank it, and he felt better.
"Where are your gold coins?" asked the Fairy.
"I lost them," said Pinocchio. But the coins were in his pocket, and at once his nose began to grow. It grew so long that he could not turn round in the room.
"Why is my nose growing?" he cried.

"Because you told a lie," said the Fairy. "There are two kinds of lies. Some lies have short legs, and some lies have long noses. Yours is a long nose." Pinocchio cried and cried. The Fairy called a hundred woodpeckers, and they made his nose small again. At last he told the truth, and the Fairy sent him home to his father.

On the road he met the Fox and the Cat again. They took him to the Field of Miracles. He dug a hole and planted his coins. Then he went away for twenty minutes. The Fox and the Cat came back, dug up the coins and ran away. When Pinocchio came back, there was no tree. He had lost everything.

He went to a judge, but the judge heard how the puppet was robbed and put him in prison for four months. When he came out, he went to look for the white house. He found only a stone with these words: "Here lies the Fairy with blue hair, who died of sorrow because her Pinocchio left her." Pinocchio cried and cried.
## Into the Sea

A pigeon passed by. "Your father is building a little boat," it said. "He wants to cross the sea and look for you in America. Today he is on the beach." Pinocchio flew on the pigeon's back to the shore. A huge storm was coming. He saw a little boat among the high waves, and then he saw nothing.

Pinocchio swam for a long time. In the morning he came to an island where kind people lived, and the Fairy lived there too, as a beautiful woman. "Now I will be a good boy," he said. "I will go to school and work. I want to be a real boy."
"If you do this," said the Fairy, "you will become a real boy."

For a time Pinocchio was good. He went to school and he learned to read. But a boy called Candlewick was his best friend. "Come with me to the Land of Toys," Candlewick said one day. "There are no schools there, no books, no teachers. We play all day long, and the holidays last for ever."

Pinocchio forgot his promise. In the night a big cart came for them, and it was full of boys, pulled by donkeys. In the Land of Toys they played games and made noise all day. For five months they never opened a book.

One morning Pinocchio woke up and felt his head. He had two long ears, and they were donkey's ears! Then his hands and feet became hooves, and he grew a tail. He tried to cry, but he could only say "hee-haw". Candlewick became a donkey too.

A man sold Pinocchio to a circus. He learned to dance and jump through hoops. But one day he hurt his leg, and the circus man sold him again. His new owner wanted to make a drum from his skin. He tied a stone to his neck and threw him into the sea.

But under the sea, the fish ate all the donkey skin. When they finished, only the wooden puppet was left. Pinocchio swam away, happy to be a puppet again. Then a huge shark came out of the water, as big as a house, and swallowed him in one bite.
## Inside the Terrible Shark

Pinocchio fell down into the dark. It was like a big, black cave. He walked and walked. At last he saw a small light far away. He went towards it, and he found a little table with a candle, and next to it sat an old man with white hair. It was Geppetto!

"Father!" cried Pinocchio. The old man could not believe his eyes. They kissed and cried and laughed together. Geppetto told him that the shark had swallowed his boat two years before. He was still alive because of a big ship that the shark had swallowed too. There were candles and food on it. But now the food and the candles were nearly finished.

"We must escape tonight," said Pinocchio. "The shark is old and sleeps with his mouth open." Geppetto could not swim well, so Pinocchio took him on his shoulders. They crept slowly through the dark. They passed the shark's tongue and came out through his big teeth.

The sea was dark and the shore was far away. Pinocchio swam as hard as he could, but he was getting tired. Then a tuna fish came to help them. "Climb on my back," it said. "I will take you to the shore." Pinocchio and Geppetto were saved.
## A Real Boy

After that, Pinocchio was a different puppet. Geppetto was weak and sick, so Pinocchio worked all day. He carried water from a well and he learned to make baskets. In the evening he studied at his books. He saved every coin for his father.

One night he had a dream. The Fairy came to him and kissed his forehead. "Well done, Pinocchio," she said. "Your good heart has made me happy. Boys who look after their parents in their sorrow and sickness are always loved, even if they are not good at school. Go on like this, and you will be happy."

Pinocchio woke up in the morning and looked at himself. He was not a puppet! He was a boy, a real boy, with hands and a face and warm skin. There was a good new suit in his room and a new hat. Geppetto was well again and singing a song.

Then Pinocchio saw his old wooden body. It was sitting on a chair, with its head falling to one side and its arms hanging down. "How funny I was when I was a puppet!" he said. "And how glad I am to be a real boy now!"

quiz.q: What did Geppetto do to buy Pinocchio a school book?
quiz.explainTr: Geppetto kış olmasına rağmen tek paltosunu satıp Pinokyo'ya okul kitabı aldı.

quiz.q: What did Pinocchio do with his school book?
options: He lost it in the street
He sold it to buy a theatre ticket
He read it on the way
quiz.explainTr: Pinokyo kitabı satıp kukla tiyatrosuna bilet aldı.

quiz.q: What did the Fox and the Cat tell Pinocchio to do with his gold coins?
options: Plant them in the Field of Miracles
quiz.explainTr: Tilki ile Kedi, parasını iki katına çıkarmak için altınları Mucizeler Tarlası'na dikmesini söyledi, sonra altınları çaldı.

quiz.q: Why did Pinocchio's nose grow long in the Fairy's house?
options: He told a lie about the gold coins
quiz.explainTr: Pinokyo altınları kaybettiğini söyleyerek yalan söyledi; yalan söyleyince burnu uzadı.

quiz.q: Where did Pinocchio find Geppetto at the end of the adventure?
quiz.explainTr: Pinokyo köpekbalığı tarafından yutulunca onun karnında Geppetto'yu buldu; birlikte kaçtılar.
